newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian economist slams interest rate cut plan.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian economist slams interest rate cut plan.

text.p: An Indonesian economist has rejected as "unworkable" proposals by a senior cabinet minister for cutting interest rates, the Jakarta Post reported on Friday.
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo, one of Indonesia's most senior economists, was quoted as saying that Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie's "zig-zag" plan to reduce interest rates was unworkable.

"What is this zig-zag all about. You want to make this country bankrupt?" Djojohadikusumo was quoted as saying during a conference sponsered by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Jakarta on Thursday.
Habibie had said Indonesia could reduce its interest rates by alternately cutting rates and then allowing them to rise.
The newspaper quoted Djojohadikusumo as saying Indonesia's high interest rates could not be cut at the moment because of continued inflationary pressures.
The central bank, Bank Indonesia's latest data puts primary lending rates for working capital at 19.35 percent and for investments at 16.39 percent.
